title.zh: 卷十二 列傳第二 后妃下
title.raw: 卷十二 列傳第二 后妃下 Volume 12 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts 2

sentences.zh: 梁文獻張皇后 武德郗皇后 武丁貴嬪 武阮修容 簡文王皇后 元徐妃 敬夏太后 敬王皇后 陳武宣章皇后 文沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 宣柳皇后 後主沈皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhang the Dedicated of Liang, Empress Chi the Martial Virtue of Liang, Honored Consort Ding the Martial of Liang, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan the Martial of Liang, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang the Proclaiming Virtue of Chen Wu, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen, Empress Wang of the Deposed Emperor, Empress Liu the Proclaiming of Emperor Xuan, Empress Shen of the Last Ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter treats Empress Zhang Wenxian of Liang, Empress Chi Wude of Liang, Honored Consort Ding, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan of Liang, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang Xuan of Emperor Wu of Chen, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen of Chen, Empress Wang of the deposed emperor, Empress Liu Xuan of Emperor Xuan of Chen, and Empress Shen of the Chen last ruler.

sentences.zh: 南朝梁

translations.literal: Southern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁文獻張皇后諱尚柔，范陽方城人也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang the Dedicated of Liang — her taboo name was Shangrou — was a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang Wenxian of Liang, whose personal name was Shangrou, came from Fangcheng in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父穆之娶文帝從姑而生后。

translations.literal: Her father Muzhi married a paternal cousin by marriage of Emperor Wen and thus the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhang Muzhi had married a paternal cousin of Emperor Wen of Liang, and it was from this union that the future empress was born.

sentences.zh: 后以宋元嘉中嬪於文帝，生長沙宣武王懿、永陽昭王敷，次生武帝。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song she became a consort of Emperor Wen and bore Changsha Prince Xuanwu Yi, Prince Zhaowu of Yongyang Fu, and afterward the future Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia reign of Liu Song she entered the household of Xiao Shunzhi (Emperor Wen) as a consort, bearing Prince Yi of Changsha, titled Xuanwu, Prince Fu of Yongyang, titled Zhaowu, and later Xiao Yan, the future Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 方孕，忽見庭前昌蒲花，光采非常，驚報，侍者皆云不見。

translations.literal: While she was pregnant she suddenly saw a calamus flower in the courtyard, extraordinarily brilliant in light; startled, she reported it, but the attendants all said they saw nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while she was pregnant, she suddenly saw a calamus flower in the courtyard shining with an unearthly brilliance. Alarmed, she told the others, but every attendant insisted that nothing was there.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「常聞見昌蒲花者當富貴。

translations.literal: The empress said, "I have often heard that one who sees a calamus flower will attain great wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I have often heard that whoever sees a calamus flower is destined for wealth and high rank."

sentences.zh: 」因取吞之，是月生武帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon she picked it and swallowed it; in that month she gave birth to the future Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: She plucked the flower and swallowed it, and in that same month she gave birth to the future Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 將產之夕，后見庭內若有衣冠陪列焉。

translations.literal: On the evening when she was about to give birth, the empress saw within the courtyard as if ranks of caps and robes were arrayed in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On the night she went into labor, she saw what looked like an assembly of officials in caps and robes standing in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 次生衡陽宣王暢、義興昭長公主令嫕。

translations.literal: She next bore Hengyang Prince Xuanwang Chang and Princess Zhaochang of Yixing Lingyi.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore Xiao Chang, Prince of Hengyang, titled Xuanwang, and Princess Lingyi of Yixing, titled Zhaochang.

sentences.zh: 后宋泰始七年殂於秣陵縣同夏里舍，葬晉陵武進縣東城里山。

translations.literal: The empress died in the seventh year of Taishi at the residence in Tongxia Village, Moling county, and was buried at Dongchengli Mountain in Wujin county, Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: The empress died in 471, the seventh year of the Taishi era, at her home in Tongxia Village, Moling county, and was buried at Dongchengli Mountain in Wujin, Jinling.

sentences.zh: 天監元年五月甲辰，追上尊號為皇后，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: On day jiachen of the fifth month of the first year of Tianjian, she was posthumously honored as empress with the temple name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the fifth month in 502, the first year of Tianjian, she was posthumously elevated to empress with the temple name Xian (Dedicated).

sentences.zh: 穆之字思靜，晉司空華六世孫也。

translations.literal: Muzhi, whose courtesy name was Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Muzhi, courtesy name Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.

sentences.zh: 少方雅，有識鑒。

translations.literal: As a youth he was refined and elegant, with discernment and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was cultivated and discerning.

sentences.zh: 初為員外散騎侍郎，深被始興王浚引納。

translations.literal: He first served as Supernumerary Attendant in the Outer Retinue of Cavalries and was deeply drawn in by Prince Jun of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a supernumerary attendant in the outer retinue of cavalries and was warmly taken up by Liu Jun, Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 穆之鑒其禍萌，求為交址太守，政有異績。

translations.literal: Muzhi perceived the budding of disaster in him and requested appointment as Administrator of Jiaozhi; his administration won unusual achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi saw the disaster Liu Jun would bring and asked to be sent away as administrator of Jiaozhi, where his rule won unusual praise.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝將以為交州刺史，會病卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song was about to appoint him Inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song was on the point of making him inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子弘籍字真藝，齊初為鎮西參軍，卒於官。

translations.literal: His son Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, in the early Qi served as Staff Officer for the Army of Pacifying the West and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, served in early Qi as staff officer to the army pacifying the west and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 梁武踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Liang Wu took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Muzhi as Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Muzhi as grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 贈弘籍廷尉卿。

translations.literal: He posthumously enfeoffed Hongji as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He also posthumously enfeoffed Hongji as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 弘籍無子，從父弟弘策以子纘嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: Hongji had no sons; his collateral younger cousin Hongce had his son Zuan succeed to the line — treated separately in another biography.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji had no sons; his younger cousin Zhang Hongce had his own son Zuan continue the line — a separate biography treats them.

sentences.zh: 武德郗皇后諱徽，高平金鄉人也。

translations.literal: Empress Chi the Martial Virtue of Liang — her taboo name was Hui — was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chi Wude of Liang, personal name Hui, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 祖紹，宋國子祭酒、領東海王師。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Shao was National University Administrator and Mentor to the Prince of Donghai under Song.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Chi Shao had been national university administrator and mentor to the prince of Donghai under Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 父曄，太子舍人，早卒。

translations.literal: Her father Ye was Crown Prince's Staff Member and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chi Ye was a staff member in the crown prince's household and died young.

sentences.zh: 后母宋文帝女尋陽公主也，方娠，夢當生貴子。

translations.literal: The empress's mother was Princess Xunyang, a daughter of Emperor Wen of Song; when she was pregnant she dreamed she would bear a noble son.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother was Princess Xunyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Song; while pregnant she dreamed she would bear a child of exalted rank.

sentences.zh: 及后生，有赤光照室，器物盡明，家人怪之。

translations.literal: When the empress was born, a red light filled the chamber and every object was bright; the household was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At the empress's birth a red light filled the room until every object gleamed, and the household was struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 巫言此女光高，將有所妨，乃于水濱祓除之。

translations.literal: A shaman said this girl's radiance was too high and would bring harm, so they performed exorcism by the waterside.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman said the girl's brilliance was too strong and would bring harm, so they performed a riverbank purification rite for her.

sentences.zh: 后幼明慧，善隸書，讀史傳。

translations.literal: As a girl the empress was bright and clever, skilled in clerical script, and read histories and chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she was quick and clever, wrote a fine clerical hand, and read histories.

sentences.zh: 女工之事，無不閑習。

translations.literal: In woman's work and crafts there was nothing she did not master.
translations.idiomatic: In needlework and domestic arts there was nothing she had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 宋後廢帝將納為后，齊初，安陸王緬又欲結婚，郗氏並辭以女疾，乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Fei of the deposed Song line wanted to take her as empress; in early Qi Prince Mian of Anlu also wished to arrange a marriage — the Chi clan refused both on the pretext of the girl's illness, and the proposals ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Emperor Fei of Song wished to make her empress, and in early Qi Liu Mian, prince of Anlu, also sought her hand; the Chi family declined both matches, pleading the girl's illness, and the proposals came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊建元末，嬪于武帝，生永興公主玉姚、永世公主玉婉、永康公主玉嬛。

translations.literal: In the last years of Jianyuan of Qi she became a consort of the future Emperor Wu and bore Princesses Yongxing Yuyao, Yongshi Yuwan, and Yongkang Yuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jianyuan era she became a consort of the future Emperor Wu of Liang and bore the princesses Yuyao of Yongxing, Yuwan of Yongshi, and Yuquan of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 及武帝為雍州刺史，殂于襄陽官舍，年三十二。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Wu was Governor of Yong province, she died at the official residence in Xiangyang at age thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: While the future emperor was governor of Yong province, she died at the government quarters in Xiangyang, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 其年歸葬南徐州南東海武進縣東城裏山。

translations.literal: That same year she was returned for burial at Dongchengli Mountain, Nan Donghai commandery, Southern Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: That year her body was brought back for burial at Dongchengli Mountain in Nan Donghai, Southern Xu province.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，武帝為梁公，齊帝詔贈后為梁公妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the future Emperor Wu was Duke of Liang, the Qi emperor ordered the empress posthumously enfeoffed as Duchess of the Duke.
translations.idiomatic: In 502, the second year of Zhongxing, when Xiao Yan was duke of Liang, the Qi court posthumously enfeoffed her as his duchess.

sentences.zh: 及武帝踐阼，追崇為皇后，諡曰德。

translations.literal: When he took the throne she was further honored as empress with the temple name De.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne she was further honored as empress with the temple name De (Virtue).

sentences.zh: 陵曰修陵。

translations.literal: Her tumulus was named Xiuling.
translations.idiomatic: Her tomb was called Xiuling.

sentences.zh: 后父曄，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The empress's father Ye was posthumously enfeoffed Senior Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chi Ye was posthumously made senior grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 后酷妒忌，及終，化為龍入于後宮井，通夢於帝。

translations.literal: The empress was fiercely jealous; after her death she transformed into a dragon and entered a rear-palace well, visiting the emperor in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had been fiercely jealous; after death she was said to turn into a dragon that entered a well in the rear palace and visited the emperor in dreams.

sentences.zh: 或見形，光彩照灼。

translations.literal: Sometimes she appeared in bodily form, her brilliance dazzling.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes she showed her form, radiant and dazzling.

sentences.zh: 帝體將不安，龍輒激水騰湧。

translations.literal: When the emperor's health wavered, the dragon would stir the water into surging waves.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor's health faltered, the dragon would churn the water into surging waves.

sentences.zh: 于露井上為殿，衣服委積，常置銀鹿盧金瓶灌百味以祀之。

translations.literal: Above the exposed well they built a hall; clothes were heaped up there, and they constantly set out a silver deer-shaped bottle and a golden bottle filled with a hundred delicacies to worship her.
translations.idiomatic: They built a hall over the open well, piled garments there, and constantly set out a silver deer-shaped vessel and a golden vessel filled with a hundred delicacies as offerings.

sentences.zh: 故帝卒不置后。

translations.literal: For this reason the emperor to the end of his life never installed another empress.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the emperor never installed another empress for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 武丁貴嬪諱令光，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Ding the Martial — her taboo name was Lingguang — was a native of Qiao state.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Ding, personal name Lingguang, came from the state of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 祖父從官襄陽，因居沔北五女村，寓於劉惠明廡下。

translations.literal: Her grandfather served as an official at Xiangyang and settled north of the Han River at Wuniu Village, lodging in the shelter of Liu Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather had served at Xiangyang and settled north of the Han at Wuniu Village, living in quarters lent by Liu Huiming.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪生於樊城，初產有神光之異，紫氣滿室，故以「光」為名。

translations.literal: The honored consort was born at Fancheng; at birth there were miraculous lights and purple vapor filled the room, hence the name "Guang".
translations.idiomatic: She was born at Fancheng; at birth supernatural lights appeared and purple vapor filled the room, whence her name Guang (Light).

sentences.zh: 相者云：「當大貴」。

translations.literal: A physiognomist said, "She will attain supreme honor."
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist said, "This girl is destined for the highest honor."

sentences.zh: 少時與鄰女月下紡績，諸女並患蚊蚋，而貴嬪弗之覺也。

translations.literal: In youth she spun with neighboring girls under the moon; the other girls all suffered from mosquitoes but the honored consort felt nothing.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she spun with neighbors under the moon; the others were tormented by mosquitoes, but she felt none.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏益德將娉之，未及成，而武帝鎮樊城，嘗登樓以望，見漢濱五采如龍，下有女子擘絖，則貴嬪也。

translations.literal: Wei Yide of the village was to marry her but before the contract was complete, while the future Emperor Wu was governing Fancheng he once mounted the tower to look out and saw five-colored light over the Han like a dragon, with a woman breaking hemp threads below — it was the honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yide of the village was to marry her, but before the betrothal was settled the future Emperor Wu, then governing Fancheng, climbed a tower and saw five-colored light over the Han like a dragon, with a woman below breaking hemp — it was she.

sentences.zh: 又丁氏因人以相者言聞之於帝，帝贈以金環，納之，時年十四。

translations.literal: Also, because of a diviner's words, someone from the Ding clan reported this to the emperor, who presented her a gold ring and received her — she was then fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: When a diviner's words reached him through the Ding clan, the prince gave her a gold ring and took her in; she was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪生而有赤志在左臂，療之不滅；

translations.literal: The honored consort was born with a red mark on her left arm; treatment did not remove it.
translations.idiomatic: She had been born with a red birthmark on her left arm that no treatment could remove.

sentences.zh: 又體多疣子，至是無何並失所在。

translations.literal: She also had many warts on her body; now, for no apparent reason, both vanished.
translations.idiomatic: She had also borne many warts; now, without cause, both the mark and the warts disappeared.

sentences.zh: 德后酷忌，遇貴嬪無道，使日舂五斛，舂每中程，若有助者，被遇雖嚴，益小心祗敬。

translations.literal: Empress De was fiercely jealous and treated the honored consort cruelly, making her pound five piculs of grain daily; whenever she met the quota it seemed as if there were help — though harshly treated she only grew more careful and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Empress De was fiercely jealous and abused her, setting her to pound five piculs of grain a day; she always finished on time, as though aided, and only grew more careful and reverent under the mistreatment.

sentences.zh: 嘗於供養經案側，髣佛若見神人，心獨異之。

translations.literal: Once beside the scripture table used for offerings she seemed dimly to see a divine figure and inwardly felt there was something extraordinary about this.
translations.idiomatic: Once, beside the sutra table where she made offerings, she seemed dimly to see a divine figure and knew inwardly that she was marked for something extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪性仁恕，及居宮接馭，自下皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: The honored consort was by nature benevolent and forgiving; in the palace in receiving and managing others, those below all took joy in her.
translations.idiomatic: By nature she was gentle and forgiving; in the palace everyone beneath her took delight in her.

sentences.zh: 不好華飾，器服無珍麗。

translations.literal: She did not love ornate adornment; vessels and dress were without precious splendor.
translations.idiomatic: She cared nothing for finery; her utensils and dress held no precious ornament.

sentences.zh: 未嘗為親戚私謁。

translations.literal: She never made private entreaties on behalf of kin.
translations.idiomatic: She never used her position to seek private favors for relatives.

sentences.zh: 及武帝弘佛教，貴嬪長進蔬膳。

translations.literal: When the emperor vigorously promoted Buddhism, the honored consort advanced vegetarian meals.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor vigorously promoted Buddhism, she took the lead in offering vegetarian fare.

sentences.zh: 受戒日，甘露降於殿前，方一丈五尺。

translations.literal: On the day she received the precepts, sweet dew fell before the hall, about one zhang five chi in extent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day she received the precepts, sweet dew fell before the hall over an area about one zhang and five chi across.

sentences.zh: 帝所立經義，皆得其指歸，尤精淨名經。

translations.literal: In scriptural doctrines the emperor established, she grasped their purport; she was especially expert in the Vimalakirti Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: In the doctrinal works the emperor expounded she grasped the meaning at once and was especially versed in the Vimalakirti Sutra.

sentences.zh: 普通七年十一月庚辰，薨，移殯於東宮臨雲殿，時年四十二。

translations.literal: On day gengchen of the eleventh month, seventh year of Putong, she died; the coffin was moved to Linyun Hall in the Eastern Palace; she was forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the eleventh month in 526, the seventh year of Putong, she died; her coffin was placed in Linyun Hall in the eastern palace. She was forty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部郎張纘為哀冊文，有司奏諡曰穆，葬甯陵，祔於小廟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Secretariat Lang Zhang Zuan to compose mourning verses; the officials memorialized the temple name Mu, burial at Ning tomb, enshrined in the lesser temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Zuan of the secretariat to compose the lament; the officials proposed the temple name Mu, burial at Ningling, and enshrinement in the lesser ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 簡文即位，追崇曰太后。

translations.literal: When Jianwen took the throne she was posthumously honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen took the throne she was posthumously honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪父道遷，天監初，為曆陽太守。

translations.literal: The honored consort's father Daotian in the first years of Tianjian was Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Ding Daotian, in the first years of Tianjian, served as administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 廬陵威王之生，武帝謂之曰：「賢女復育一男。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei of Luling was born the emperor said to him, "Your worthy daughter has borne another boy."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei of Luling was born, the emperor told him, "Your worthy daughter has borne another son."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「莫道豬狗子。

translations.literal: He replied, "Don't speak of it as a pig-child."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Don't call him a pig's whelp."

sentences.zh: 」世人以為笑。

translations.literal: People at the time took this as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time laughed at the remark.

sentences.zh: 後位兗州刺史、宣城太守。

translations.literal: Later he reached the posts of Inspector of Yan province and Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to inspector of Yan province and administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，追贈太后父齊故奉朝請石靈寶散騎常侍、左衛將軍、封武康縣侯，母陳氏武康侯夫人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, they posthumously enfeoffed the empress dowager's father, the former Presentation Attendant of Qi Shi Lingbao, as Central Cavalier Attendant, Left Guard General, and Marquis of Wukang, and her mother Lady Chen as the Marchioness of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In 553, the second year of Chengsheng, they posthumously enfeoffed the empress dowager's adoptive father, the former presentation attendant of Qi Shi Lingbao, as central cavalier attendant and left guard general with the marquisate of Wukang, and her mother Lady Chen as marchioness of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 元帝徐妃諱昭佩，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan — her taboo name was Zhaopei — was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan of Liang, personal name Zhaopei, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖孝嗣，齊太尉、枝江文忠公。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Xiaosi was Grand Marshal of Qi, Duke Wenzhong of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Xu Xiaosi had been grand marshal of Qi and duke Wenzhong of Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 父緄，侍中、信武將軍。

translations.literal: Her father Wei was Palace Attendant and General of Trustworthy Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xu Wei was palace attendant and general of trustworthy martiality.

sentences.zh: 妃以天監十六年十二月拜湘東王妃，生世子方等、益昌公主含貞。

translations.literal: The consort in the twelfth month of the sixteenth year of Tianjian was invested Princess of the Xiangdong Princedom and bore the Heir Apparent Fangdeng and Princess Yichang Hanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 517, the sixteenth year of Tianjian, she was invested princess of Xiangdong and bore the heir apparent Fangdeng and Princess Hanzhen of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 妃無容質，不見禮，帝三二年一入房。

translations.literal: The consort had no beauty and received no courtesy; the emperor entered her chamber only once every two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: Plain in looks, she went without favor; the emperor visited her bed only once every two or three years.

sentences.zh: 妃以帝眇一目，每知帝將至，必為半面妝以俟，帝見則大怒而出。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was blind in one eye, whenever she knew he was coming she would paint only half her face and wait; when he saw this he would rage and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor was blind in one eye, she would paint only half her face before his visits; when he saw her he would fly into a rage and storm out.

sentences.zh: 妃性嗜酒，多洪醉，帝還房，必吐衣中。

translations.literal: The consort was fond of wine and often drank to excess; when the emperor returned to her chamber she would vomit on his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: She loved wine and often drank herself drunk; when the emperor came to her bed she would be sick on his garments.

sentences.zh: 與荊州後堂瑤光寺智遠道人私通。

translations.literal: She had illicit relations with the monk Zhiyuan of the Yaoguang Temple in the rear hall of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: She carried on an affair with the monk Zhiyuan of Yaoguang Temple in the Jing provincial rear hall.

sentences.zh: 酷妒忌，見無寵之妾，便交杯接坐。

translations.literal: Fiercely jealous, when she saw a consort without favor she would sit knee to knee with her sharing cups.
translations.idiomatic: Violently jealous, she would sit knee to knee and pass cups with any unfavored consort she saw.

sentences.zh: 才覺有娠者，即手加刀刃。

translations.literal: As soon as she sensed anyone was pregnant she would personally apply a blade.
translations.idiomatic: The moment she detected a pregnancy she would take a blade to the woman herself.

sentences.zh: 帝左右暨季江有姿容，又與淫通。

translations.literal: Ji Jiang of the emperor's attendants was handsome in appearance, and she also had illicit relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jiang, one of the emperor's attendants, was handsome, and she took him as a lover as well.

sentences.zh: 季江每歎曰：「柏直狗雖老猶能獵，蕭溧陽馬雖老猶駿，徐娘雖老猶尚多情。

translations.literal: Ji Jiang would sigh each time, "Bo Zhi's dog, though old, can still hunt; Xiao of Liyang's horse, though old, is still swift; though Lady Xu is old, she is still full of passion."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jiang would sigh, "Bo Zhi's dog may be old but still hunts; the horse of the Xiao of Liyang may be old but still runs; and Lady Xu, though old, is still amorous."

sentences.zh: 」時有賀徽者美色，妃要之於普賢尼寺，書白角枕為詩相贈答。

translations.literal: There was then He Hui, a man of beauty; the consort summoned him to Puxian Nunnery and they exchanged poems written on white-horn pillows.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the handsome He Hui; she summoned him to Puxian Nunnery, and they exchanged poems written on pillows of white horn.

sentences.zh: 既而貞惠世子方諸母王氏寵愛，未幾而終，元帝歸咎於妃；

translations.literal: Before long the mother of the Heir of Pure Favor Fangzhu, Lady Wang, who was favored, died not long after; Emperor Yuan blamed the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lady Wang, mother of the heir of pure favor Fangzhu, who had been favored, died; Emperor Yuan laid the blame on the consort.

sentences.zh: 及方等死，愈見疾。

translations.literal: When Fangdeng died she was hated all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangdeng died as well, his hatred for her only deepened.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，遂逼令自殺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing she was compelled to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: In 549, the third year of Taiqing, he forced her to kill herself.

sentences.zh: 妃知不免，乃透井死。

translations.literal: Knowing she could not escape, she threw herself down a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, she threw herself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 帝以屍還徐氏，謂之出妻。

translations.literal: The emperor returned her corpse to the Xu clan, calling her a divorced wife.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent her body back to the Xu clan, treating her as a wife who had been cast out.

sentences.zh: 葬江陵瓦官寺。

translations.literal: She was buried at Waguan Temple in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Waguan Temple in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 帝制金樓子述其淫行。

translations.literal: The emperor in his Golden Louzi recorded her licentious conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set down her debauchery in his Golden Louzi.

sentences.zh: 初，妃嫁夕，車至西州，而疾風大起，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: At first, on the evening of the consort's marriage, when the carriage reached Xizhou a fierce wind arose, tearing off roofs and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: When she first married, as the bridal carriage reached Xizhou a violent wind sprang up, ripping off roofs and snapping trees.

sentences.zh: 無何，雪霰交下，帷簾皆白。

translations.literal: Before long, snow and hail fell together and the curtains all turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Soon snow and hail fell together until the curtains were white.

sentences.zh: 及長還之日，又大雷震西州聽事兩柱俱碎。

translations.literal: On the day of her long return visit there was again a great thunderclap that shattered both pillars of the audience hall in Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of her formal visit home thunder again split both pillars of the Xizhou audience hall.

sentences.zh: 帝以為不祥，后果不終婦道。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded these as ill omens, and in the end she did not fulfill a wife's duty to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took these as evil portents, and in the end she failed to keep the way of a wife.

sentences.zh: 南朝陳

translations.literal: Southern Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Chen.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，后下令黜廢帝為臨海王，命宣帝嗣立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda the empress issued an order deposing the emperor as Prince of Linhai and commanding Emperor Xuan to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In 567, the second year of Guangda, the empress issued an edict deposing the emperor as prince of Linhai and ordering Emperor Xuan to succeed.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，復為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian she again became empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In 569, the first year of Taijian, she again became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 二年三月丙申，崩於紫極殿，時年六十五。

translations.literal: On day bingshen of the third month of the second year she died in the Ziji Hall at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the third month in 570, the second year of Taijian, she died in Ziji Hall, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 遺令喪事並從儉約，諸饋奠不用牲牢。

translations.literal: Her testament ordered the funeral to be entirely frugal and that offerings should not use sacrificial livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Her final instructions required a spare funeral and forbade livestock in the offerings.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，群臣上諡曰宣，祔葬萬安陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year the ministers proposed the temple name Xuan, and she was buried with joint honors at Wan'an tomb.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month the ministers proposed the temple name Xuan, and she was buried with her husband at Wan'anling.

sentences.zh: 后親屬無在朝者，唯本族兄鈕洽官至中散大夫。

translations.literal: None of the empress's kin held office at court; only a clansman on her mother's side, Niu Qia, reached Central Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: No member of the empress's family held court office; only a maternal clansman, Niu Qia, rose to central cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 文沈皇后諱妙容，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Empress Shen of Emperor Wen — her taboo name was Miaorong — was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shen of Emperor Wen of Chen, personal name Miaorong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父法深，梁安前中錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Her father Fashen was Central Recorder and Staff Officer under Anqian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shen Fashen had been central recorder and staff officer under Xiao An, prince of Anqian.

sentences.zh: 后年十歲余，以梁大同中歸於文帝。

translations.literal: When the empress was a little over ten, in the Datong era of Liang she was given in marriage to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Before she was eleven, during the Datong era of Liang, she was married to Chen Qian, the future Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 武帝之討侯景，文帝時在吳興，及后並被收，景平，乃獲免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Hou Jing, Emperor Wen was then in Wuxing; the empress was seized together with him, and when Jing was pacified they were released.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang marched against Hou Jing, the future Emperor Wen was in Wuxing; she was captured with him and not freed until Hou Jing fell.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，后為臨川王妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, the empress became Princess of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, she became princess of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, she became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband became Emperor Wen of Chen, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 追贈后父法深光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，封建城縣侯，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: They posthumously enfeoffed the empress's father Fashen as Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jiancheng, with the temple name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Fashen was posthumously made grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord, enfeoffed as marquis of Jiancheng with the temple name Gong.

sentences.zh: 追贈后母高為綏安縣君，諡曰定。

translations.literal: They posthumously enfeoffed the empress's mother Gao as Lady of Sui'an commandery, with the temple name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Gao was posthumously made lady of Sui'an with the temple name Ding.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰安德。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Ande.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor succeeded, she was honored as empress dowager and dwelt in Ande Palace.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝與僕射到仲舉、舍人劉師知等，並受遺輔政。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan, together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Dao Zhongju and Staff Member Liu Shizhi and others, all received the testamentary charge to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Xu, the future Emperor Xuan, shared the regency with vice director of the secretariat Dao Zhongju, staff member Liu Shizhi, and others under the late emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 師知與仲舉恒居禁中，參決眾事，而宣帝為揚州刺史，與左右三百人，入居尚書省。

translations.literal: Shizhi and Zhongju constantly dwelt within the forbidden quarters, participating in deciding all affairs, while Emperor Xuan was Governor of Yang province and with some three hundred attendants entered and dwelt in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi and Zhongju lived inside the palace and decided every matter, while Emperor Xuan remained in the secretariat as governor of Yang with three hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 師知忌宣帝權重，矯敕令還東府理州務。

translations.literal: Shizhi resented Emperor Xuan's weight of authority and by a forged edict ordered him to return to the eastern headquarters to manage provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of his power, Shizhi forged an edict sending him back to the eastern headquarters to handle provincial business.

sentences.zh: 宣帝將出，毛喜止帝曰：「今若出外，便受制於人，如曹爽願作富家公不可得也。

translations.literal: As Emperor Xuan was about to go out, Mao Xi stopped the emperor and said, "If you go out now, you will be controlled by others — like Cao Shuang, you will not be able even to wish to be a rich household head."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Mao Xi stopped him and said, "Once you step outside you will be at their mercy — like Cao Shuang, you will not even be able to play the wealthy private citizen."

sentences.zh: 」宣帝乃稱疾，召師知留與語，使毛喜先入，言之於后。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan thereupon claimed illness, summoned Shizhi to stay and talk with him, and sent Mao Xi in first to speak to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan feigned illness, kept Shizhi talking, and sent Mao Xi ahead to speak with the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「今伯宗年幼，政事並委二郎，此非我意。

translations.literal: The empress said, "Now Bozong is young; to entrust all government to the Second Lord is not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Bozong is still a child; to hand all government to the second lord is not what I intend."

sentences.zh: 」喜又言於廢帝，廢帝曰：「此自師知等所為，非朕意也。

translations.literal: Xi also spoke to the deposed emperor; the deposed emperor said, "This is what Shizhi and the others have done — it is not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Xi also spoke to the reigning emperor, who said, "This is Shizhi's doing, not mine."

sentences.zh: 」喜出報宣帝，帝因囚師知。

translations.literal: Xi went out and reported to Emperor Xuan; the emperor thereupon imprisoned Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi reported back to Emperor Xuan, who at once had Shizhi arrested.

sentences.zh: 自入見后及帝，極陳師知之短。

translations.literal: He himself entered to see the empress and the emperor and set forth Shizhi's faults to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in to the empress dowager and the emperor and laid out Shizhi's crimes in full.

sentences.zh: 仍自草敕請畫，以師知付廷尉，其夜於獄賜死。

translations.literal: He thereupon himself drafted the edict requesting the brush and handed Shizhi over to the Minister of Justice; that night in prison he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the edict himself and had Shizhi sent to the minister of justice; that night Shizhi was ordered to die in prison.

sentences.zh: 自是政歸宣帝。

translations.literal: From this time government returned to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on power passed to Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 后憂悶，計無所出，乃密賂宦者蔣裕，令誘建安人張安國使據郡反，冀因此圖帝。

translations.literal: The empress was anxious and depressed, with no plan; she secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to induce Zhang Anguo of Jian'an to raise the commandery in rebellion, hoping thereby to strike at the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed and at a loss, she secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to incite Zhang Anguo of Jian'an to rebel, hoping to turn the tables on the emperor.

sentences.zh: 安國事發被誅，時后左右近侍頗知其事，后恐連逮黨與，並殺之。

translations.literal: When Anguo's affair was exposed he was executed; at that time the empress's close attendants knew much of the matter, and fearing their associates would be implicated she had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered Anguo was executed; many of her attendants knew too much, and fearing exposure she had them killed as well.

sentences.zh: 后兄欽，襲爵建城侯，位尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Qin inherited the marquisate of Jiancheng and held the post of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Shen Qin inherited the marquisate of Jiancheng and served as left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 欽素無伎能，奉己而已。

translations.literal: Qin throughout lacked ability and only looked after himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had no talent and cared only for his own comfort.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died his temple name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the temple name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子觀嗣，頗有學識，官至御史中丞。

translations.literal: His son Guan succeeded, quite learned, and reached the post of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen Guan succeeded him, a man of learning who rose to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 宣柳皇后諱敬言，河東解縣人也。

translations.literal: Empress Liu the Proclaiming of Emperor Xuan — her taboo name was Jingyan — was a native of Jie county in Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu Xuan of Emperor Xuan of Chen, personal name Jingyan, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖世隆，祖惲，父偃，並有傳。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather was Shilong, her grandfather Yun, her father Yan — all have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Liu Shilong, grandfather Liu Yun, and father Liu Yan each have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 后九歲，幹理家事，有若成人。

translations.literal: At nine the empress managed the household affairs as if she were an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At nine she already ran the household like a grown woman.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，后與弟盼往江陵，依梁元帝，帝以長城公主故，待遇甚厚，以配宣帝。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Hou Jing, the empress and her younger brother Pan went to Jiangling and relied on Emperor Yuan of Liang; because of the Princess of Changcheng he treated them very generously and gave her in marriage to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion she and her brother Pan fled to Jiangling and were sheltered by Emperor Yuan of Liang, who, for the sake of the princess of Changcheng, treated them well and gave her to the future Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，后生後主于江陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng the empress bore the last ruler at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In 553, the second year of Chengsheng, she bore the future last ruler at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 及魏克江陵，宣帝遷于關右，后與後主俱留穰城。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Emperor Xuan was moved to the west; the empress and the last ruler both remained at Rang city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, Emperor Xuan was taken west; she and the last ruler stayed behind at Rang.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，與後主還朝，后為安成王妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianchen they returned to court with the last ruler; the empress became Princess of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 563, the second year of Tianchen, they returned to the Chen court and she became princess of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 后美姿容，身長七尺二寸，手垂過膝。

translations.literal: The empress had beautiful features; her body was seven chi two cun in height and her hands hung below her knees.
translations.idiomatic: She was beautiful, stood seven chi two cun tall, and her hands reached below her knees.

sentences.zh: 後主沈皇后諱婺華，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Empress Shen of the Last Ruler — her taboo name was Wuhua — was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shen Wuhua of the Chen last ruler came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父君理自有傳。

translations.literal: Her father Junli has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shen Junli has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 后母即武帝女會稽穆公主，早亡。

translations.literal: The empress's mother was the Princess of Kuaiji the Reverent, a daughter of Emperor Wu, who died young.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Princess Kuaiji the Reverent, a daughter of Emperor Wu of Liang, who died early.

sentences.zh: 時后尚幼，而毀瘠過甚。

translations.literal: The empress was still young but her emaciation from mourning was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a child, she wasted away in mourning beyond what was expected.

sentences.zh: 及服畢，每歲時朔望，恒獨坐涕泣，哀動左右，內外敬異焉。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, at each season's new and full moon she would sit alone weeping; her grief moved those about her, and inside and outside all regarded her with respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended she wept alone at every new and full moon, moving all who saw her; kin and court alike marveled at her.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，拜為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian she was invested as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In 569, the first year of Taijian, she was invested crown princess.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the last ruler took the throne she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the last ruler took the throne she became empress.

sentences.zh: 后性端靜，有識量，寡嗜欲，聰敏強記，涉獵經史，工書翰。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature upright and quiet, with judgment and measure, few desires, clever and with a strong memory; she read widely in the classics and histories and was skilled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, quiet, and discerning, with few desires, she was quick-witted and well read in the classics and histories and wrote a fine hand.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，而后父君理卒，居憂處別殿，哀毀逾禮。

translations.literal: While the last ruler was in the eastern palace, the empress's father Junli died; she dwelt in a separate hall in mourning and her grief exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: While her husband was crown prince her father Junli died; she mourned in a separate hall with a grief that exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 後主遇后既薄，而張貴妃有寵，總後宮之政，后澹然未嘗有所忌怨。

translations.literal: The last ruler's treatment of the empress was always cold, while Honored Consort Zhang was favored and held sway over the rear palace; the empress remained placid and never showed jealousy or resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The last ruler cared little for her while Zhang Guifei ruled the inner quarters; she remained calm and never showed envy.

sentences.zh: 而身居儉約，衣服無錦繡之飾，左右近侍才百許人，唯尋閱圖史及釋典為事。

translations.literal: She herself lived in thrift; her clothes had no brocade or embroidery; her close attendants numbered only about a hundred, and she occupied herself solely with histories and Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: She lived plainly, wore no brocade, kept barely a hundred attendants, and passed her days with histories and Buddhist texts.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇歲旱，自暴而誦佛經，應時雨降。

translations.literal: Once when drought came she exposed herself and chanted Buddhist scriptures, and rain fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once during a drought she exposed herself and chanted sutras, and rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 無子，養孫姬子胤為己子。

translations.literal: Having no son, she adopted the son of a palace woman, Ziyin, as her own child.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, she adopted the palace woman's son Ziyin as her own.

sentences.zh: 數上書諫爭，後主將廢之，而立張貴妃，會國亡不果，乃與後主俱入長安。

translations.literal: She repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating; the last ruler was about to depose her and establish Honored Consort Zhang, but when the state perished the plan was not carried out, and she entered Chang'an together with the last ruler.
translations.idiomatic: She remonstrated again and again; the last ruler meant to depose her for Zhang Guifei, but the fall of Chen prevented it, and she followed him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及後主薨，后自為哀辭，文甚酸切。

translations.literal: When the last ruler died the empress herself composed the lament; the text was very bitter and keen.
translations.idiomatic: After his death she wrote the lament herself, its words sharp with grief.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝每巡幸，恒令從駕。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Yang of Sui went on tour he always ordered her to follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On every tour of Emperor Yang of Sui she was ordered to accompany the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝被殺，后自廣陵過江，於毗陵天靜寺為尼，名觀音。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was killed the empress crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and at Tianjing Temple in Piling became a nun, taking the name Guanyin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang's death she crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and took the tonsure at Tianjing Temple in Piling under the name Guanyin.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初卒。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan era she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died early in the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃名麗華，兵家女也。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhang, named Lihua, was the daughter of a military family.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guifei, personal name Lihua, came from a soldier's family.

sentences.zh: 父兄以織席為業。

translations.literal: Her father and brothers took weaving rush mats as their trade.
translations.idiomatic: Her father and brothers wove rush mats for a living.

sentences.zh: 後主為太子，以選入宮。

translations.literal: When the last ruler was crown prince she was chosen to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the last ruler was crown prince she was selected for the palace.

sentences.zh: 時龔貴嬪為良娣，貴妃年十歲，為之給使。

translations.literal: At that time Honored Consort Gong was a lady of the heir apparent; the honored consort was ten years old and served her.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Guifei was then a lady of the heir apparent's household; Lihua, ten years old, attended her.

sentences.zh: 後主見而悅之，因得幸，遂有娠，生太子深。

translations.literal: The last ruler saw her and was pleased; he gained her favor and she became pregnant, bearing the crown prince Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince noticed her, took her to bed, and she bore the heir apparent Shen.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，拜為貴妃。

translations.literal: When the last ruler took the throne she was appointed Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he became emperor she was made honored consort.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，甚被寵遇。

translations.literal: By nature clever and intelligent, she was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick, she won extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 後主始以始興王叔陵之亂，被傷，臥於承香殿。

translations.literal: At first, because of the disorder of Prince Shuling of Shixing, the last ruler was wounded and lay ill in Chenxiang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After the uprising of Prince Shuling of Shixing wounded him, the last ruler lay ill in Chenxiang Hall.

sentences.zh: 時諸姬並不得進，唯貴妃侍焉。

translations.literal: At that time none of the consorts could approach; only the honored consort attended him.
translations.idiomatic: No other consort was admitted; only Zhang Guifei nursed him.

sentences.zh: 而柳太后猶居柏梁殿，即皇后之正殿也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Liu still dwelt in Bailiang Hall, the very main hall of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu still lived in Bailiang Hall, the empress's proper hall.

sentences.zh: 而沈皇后素無寵於後主，不得侍疾，別居求賢殿。

translations.literal: Empress Shen had always lacked the last ruler's favor and could not attend his illness, dwelling separately at Qiuxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shen had never been loved and could not attend him, remaining at Qiuxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，乃於光昭殿前起臨春、結綺、望仙三閣，高數十丈，並數十間。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide they raised before Guangzhao Hall the three pavilions Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian, several tens of zhang high and with several tens of rooms.
translations.idiomatic: In 586, the second year of Zhide, they built the Linchun, Jieqi, and Wangxian pavilions before Guangzhao Hall, each tens of zhang high with dozens of rooms.

sentences.zh: 其窗牖、壁帶、縣楣、欄檻之類，皆以沈檀香為之，又飾以金玉，間以珠翠，外施珠簾。

translations.literal: Their windows, wall bands, hanging beams, and balustrades were all of agarwood incense; they were further adorned with gold and jade and set with pearls and kingfisher feathers, with pearl curtains hung outside.
translations.idiomatic: Windows, beams, and railings were of agarwood, inlaid with gold, jade, pearls, and kingfisher, and hung with pearl curtains.

sentences.zh: 內有寶床寶帳，其服玩之屬，瑰麗皆近古未有。

translations.literal: Within were precious couches and canopies; among garments and playthings, the splendor was nearly unmatched in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were jeweled beds and canopies and ornaments of a splendor seldom seen before.

sentences.zh: 每微風暫至，香聞數里，朝日初照，光映後庭。

translations.literal: Whenever a slight breeze passed, the fragrance was smelled for several li; when the morning sun first shone, light flooded the rear courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: A light breeze carried perfume for miles; at sunrise light filled the rear court.

sentences.zh: 其下積石為山，引水為池，植以奇樹，雜以花藥。

translations.literal: Below they piled stone into mountains, led water into pools, planted rare trees, and mixed in flowers and herbs.
translations.idiomatic: Below they piled rockeries, drew channels, and planted exotic trees and flowers.

sentences.zh: 後主自居臨春閣，張貴妃居結綺閣，龔、孔二貴嬪居望仙閣，並復道交相往來。

translations.literal: The last ruler himself dwelt in Linchun Pavilion; Honored Consort Zhang dwelt in Jieqi Pavilion; the two honored consorts Gong and Kong dwelt in Wangxian Pavilion, with covered ways connecting them for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived in Linchun, Zhang in Jieqi, Gong and Kong in Wangxian, linked by covered walkways.

sentences.zh: 又有王、季二美人，張、薛二淑媛，袁昭儀、何婕妤、江修容等七人，並有寵，遞代以遊其上。

translations.literal: There were also the two beauties Wang and Ji, the two fair ladies Zhang and Xue, Lady Yuan the Bright Deportment, Lady He the Talented Fairness, Lady Jiang the Cultivated Countenance, and seven others — all favored — who in turn sported upon the pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: The beauties Wang and Ji, the fair ladies Zhang and Xue, Ladies Yuan, He, and Jiang, and seven others all shared his favor and took turns on the terraces.

sentences.zh: 以宮人有文學者袁大舍等為女學士。

translations.literal: They took palace women with literary talent, such as Yuan Dashe, as female academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women of letters such as Yuan Dashe were made female academicians.

sentences.zh: 後主每引賓客，對貴妃等游宴，則使諸貴人及女學士與狎客共賦新詩，互相贈答。

translations.literal: Whenever the last ruler led guests to feast and roam with the honored consort and others, he would have the various noble ladies and female academicians compose new poems with intimate guests, exchanging them as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets with Zhang and the others he had court ladies and female scholars trade new poems with his intimates.

sentences.zh: 采其尤豔麗者，以為曲調，被以新聲。

translations.literal: They selected the most gorgeous lines to serve as lyrics and set them to new melodies.
translations.idiomatic: The loveliest lines were set to new tunes.

sentences.zh: 選宮女有容色者以千百數，令習而歌之，分部疊進，持以相樂。

translations.literal: They chose palace women of pleasing appearance by the thousands and hundreds, ordered them to learn and sing, divided into groups and advancing in layers, holding one another in mutual delight.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of pretty palace women learned the songs and sang them in ranks for his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 其曲有玉樹後庭花、臨春樂等。

translations.literal: Among the tunes were Jade Tree in the Rear Court and Linchun Music.
translations.idiomatic: Among the songs were Jade Tree in the Rear Court and Linchun Music.

sentences.zh: 其略云：「璧月夜夜滿，瓊樹朝朝新。

translations.literal: In brief they run: "The jade moon is full night after night; the jeweled trees are fresh morning after morning."
translations.idiomatic: One refrain ran, "The jade moon is full each night; the jeweled trees are fresh each dawn."

sentences.zh: 」大抵所歸，皆美張貴妃、孔貴嬪之容色。

translations.literal: For the most part what they aimed at was to praise the beauty of Honored Consort Zhang and Honored Consort Kong.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly all praised the beauty of Zhang and Kong Guifei.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃髪長七尺，鬒黑如漆，其光可鑒。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhang's hair was seven chi long, raven-black as lacquer, its luster mirror-bright.
translations.idiomatic: Her hair was seven chi long, black as lacquer and bright as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 特聰慧，有神彩，進止閑華，容色端麗。

translations.literal: Especially clever and intelligent, with divine spirit; her advance and pause were leisurely and splendid, her countenance upright and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: Unusually clever and spirited, she moved with grace and her face was fair and composed.

sentences.zh: 每瞻視眄睞，光彩溢目，照映左右。

translations.literal: Whenever she glanced and looked askance, radiance overflowed her eyes and shone on those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Each glance spilled light from her eyes onto those beside her.

sentences.zh: 嘗於閣上靚妝，臨於軒檻，宮中遙望，飄若神仙。

translations.literal: Once on the pavilion she made up her face finely and leaned on the balustrade; gazing from afar within the palace, she floated like an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Once, dressed at the railing of a pavilion, she seemed a spirit to those watching from afar.

sentences.zh: 才辯強記，善候人主顏色。

translations.literal: Talented in debate with a strong memory, she was skilled at observing the sovereign's expression.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent and quick to remember, she read the emperor's mood with ease.

sentences.zh: 薦諸宮女，後宮咸德之，競言其善。

translations.literal: She recommended palace women; the rear palace all thanked her and vied in speaking of her goodness.
translations.idiomatic: She spoke for other palace women, and the inner quarters all praised her kindness.

sentences.zh: 又工厭魅之術，假鬼道以惑後主。

translations.literal: She was also skilled in sorcery and witchcraft and by false ghostly ways deluded the last ruler.
translations.idiomatic: She also practiced sorcery and deluded him with sham spirit rites.

sentences.zh: 置淫祀于宮中，聚諸女巫使之鼓舞。

translations.literal: She set up licentious sacrifices within the palace and gathered shamanesses to make them drum and dance.
translations.idiomatic: She set up illicit shrines in the palace and gathered witches to dance and chant.

sentences.zh: 時後主怠於政事，百司啟奏，並因宦者蔡臨兒、李善度進請，後主倚隱囊，置張貴妃于膝上共決之。

translations.literal: At that time the last ruler was slack in government affairs; memorials from the hundred offices all entered through the eunuchs Cai Lin'er and Li Shandu; the last ruler leaned on a bolster with Honored Consort Zhang on his knees jointly deciding them.
translations.idiomatic: Neglecting government, he let memorials pass through eunuchs Cai Lin'er and Li Shandu while he lay back with Zhang Guifei on his knee deciding them.

sentences.zh: 李、蔡所不能記者，貴妃並為疏條，無所遺脫。

translations.literal: What Li and Cai could not remember, the honored consort would set out in summary with nothing omitted.
translations.idiomatic: What the eunuchs forgot she summarized without omission.

sentences.zh: 因參訪外事，人間有一言一事，貴妃必先知白之，由是益加寵異，冠絕後庭。

translations.literal: Because she also investigated external affairs, whenever there was a word or affair among the people the honored consort would first know and report it; thereby favor increased still more, surpassing all the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on the world outside as well; whatever was said in the streets she reported first, and her favor surpassed every rival.

sentences.zh: 而後宮之家，不遵法度，有絓於理者，但求恩于貴妃，貴妃則令李、蔡先啟其事，而后從容為言之。

translations.literal: When families of the rear palace did not observe the law and were entangled in reason, they need only seek favor from the honored consort; the honored consort would have Li and Cai first raise the matter, then calmly speak of it for them.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of consorts who broke the law sought her favor; she had Li and Cai bring the case up, then spoke for them at leisure.

sentences.zh: 大臣有不從者，因而譖之，言無不聽。

translations.literal: When great ministers did not comply, she thereupon slandered them, and her words were never not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who resisted were slandered, and the emperor never refused her.

sentences.zh: 於是張、孔之權，熏灼四方，內外宗族，多被引用，大臣執政，亦從風而靡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the power of Zhang and Kong scorched the four quarters; inside and outside their clans were widely employed, and great ministers holding government also bent with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang and Kong clans blazed with power east and west; ministers bent to their wind.

sentences.zh: 閹宦便佞之徒，內外交結，轉相引進。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and fawning men, inside and outside interlinked, introduced one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and flatterers wove a web of mutual promotion.

sentences.zh: 賄賂公行，賞罰無常，綱紀瞀亂矣。

translations.literal: Bribery ran openly; rewards and punishments had no constancy; the bonds of discipline were confused and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes flowed freely, rewards and punishments lost all rule, and government collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 及隋軍克台城，貴妃與後主俱入井，隋軍出之，晉王廣命斬之於青溪中橋。

translations.literal: When the Sui army captured Taicheng, the honored consort and the last ruler both entered a well; the Sui army drew them out, and Prince of Jin Guang ordered her beheaded at the Zhongqiao on Qing Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui took Taicheng she and the last ruler hid in a well; pulled out, Yang Guang had her beheaded at Zhongqiao on Qing Stream.

sentences.zh: 論曰：飲食男女，人之大欲存焉，故聖人順于人情而為之度。

translations.literal: The discussion says: Food and drink, man and woman — in these the great desires of human beings reside; therefore the sages accord with human feeling and set measures for them.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Food and sex are mankind's deepest urges; the sages therefore measure conduct to human feeling.

sentences.zh: 王宮六列，士室二等，皆隨事升降，以立節文。

translations.literal: The royal palace's six ranks and the scholar's two grades all rise and fall with circumstances to establish regulated forms.
translations.idiomatic: The six ranks of the royal palace and the two grades of the gentry rise and fall with circumstance to set proper limits.

sentences.zh: 若夫義篤閫闈，政刑邦國，古先哲王有以之致化矣。

translations.literal: If righteousness is solid within the inner gates and government and punishments govern the state, the ancient sage kings by this brought transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness rules the household and law the state, sage kings of old achieved order thereby.

sentences.zh: 夫后妃專夕，配以德升，姬嬙並禦，進非色幸，欲使情有覃被，愛罔偏流，專貞內表，妖蠱外息，乃可以輔興君德，燮理陰政。

translations.literal: When empresses and consorts monopolize the night and are elevated by virtue, when concubines share the bedchamber and advance not through beauty's favor — wishing that affection be broadly spread and love not flow in bias, with chaste fidelity within and seductive witchcraft stilled without — then one may assist in raising the ruler's virtue and harmonizing yin governance.
translations.idiomatic: When empresses are chosen for virtue, concubines for character rather than looks, and favor is shared without partiality, inner fidelity and outer restraint can support the throne and harmonize the inner court.

sentences.zh: 宋氏因晉之舊典，聘納有方，俔天作儷，必四嶽之後。

translations.literal: The Song house followed Jin's old statutes: betrothal had its forms, and matching Heaven in marriage required descendants of the Four Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed Jin's marriage code: betrothal had fixed forms, and empresses came from the great ministerial lines.

sentences.zh: 自元嘉以降，內職稍繁，所選止於軍署，徵引極乎廝皁，非若晉氏采擇，濫及冠冕者焉。

translations.literal: From the Yuanjia era onward inner offices grew somewhat numerous; selection was limited to military headquarters, recruitment reaching as far as menials — not like the Jin house's choosing, which overflowed even to the capped and belted.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanjia the inner staff grew; candidates came only from army offices, even from servants — unlike Jin, whose choices had reached the gentry.

sentences.zh: 而愛止帷房，權無外授，戚屬餼賚，歲時不過肴漿，斯為美矣。

translations.literal: Yet love was confined to the bedchamber and authority was not delegated outward; kin received gifts at the seasons no more than broth — this was beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet favor stayed within the chambers, power never left the palace, and kin received no more than simple gifts at the seasons — a restraint to admire.

sentences.zh: 及文帝之傾惑潘嫗，謀及婦人；

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was led astray by Lady Pan, his plots reached even to women.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Song was bewitched by Lady Pan, even women were drawn into his plots.

sentences.zh: 大明之淪沒殷姬，並后匹嫡，其為喪敗，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: In the Daming era the ruin of Lady Yin, with a consort matching the primary wife — their bringing ruin was already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Lady Yin's fall and a consort raised to equal the empress brought ruin already extreme.

sentences.zh: 齊氏孝、昭二后，並有賢明之訓，惜乎早世，不得母臨萬國。

translations.literal: The two empresses Xiao and Zhao of Qi both had teachings of worth and wisdom; alas that they died young and could not mother the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Xiao and Zhao of Qi were both wise; pity that they died young and never ruled as mothers of the state.

sentences.zh: 有婦人焉，空慕周典，禎符顯瑞，徒萃徽名。

translations.literal: There was a certain woman who vainly admired the Zhou rites; auspicious talismans and manifest omens only heaped empty glorious names.
translations.idiomatic: One woman merely aped Zhou ritual while omens heaped empty glory on her name.

sentences.zh: 高皇受命，宮禁貶約，衣不文繡，色無紅采，永巷貧空，有同素室。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor received the mandate, palace prohibitions were cheap and few; clothes had no patterned embroidery, colors no red or cinnabar; the long lanes were poor and empty, like plain rooms.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Di of Qi took power, the palace was austere: no embroidered robes, no bright red, the women's quarters as bare as a common house.

sentences.zh: 武帝嗣位，運藉休平，壽昌前興，鳳華晚構，香柏文檉，花梁繡柱，雕金鏤寶，照燭房帷，趙瑟吳趨，承閑奏曲，事由私蓄，無損國儲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu succeeded, fortune rested on peaceful times; Shouchang rose early, Fenghua was built late — fragrant cypress and patterned toona, flowered beams and embroidered pillars, carved gold and chased jewels lighting the bed curtains; Zhao zithers and Wu dances performed at leisure — all from private stores, without harm to the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi enjoyed peace; early omens and late splendor filled the chambers with carved beams, incense wood, gold, and jewels, with music at hand — paid from private funds, not the treasury.

sentences.zh: 明帝統業，矯情儉陋，奉己之制，曾莫雲改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming unified the inheritance he corrected emotion into frugal ugliness; the regulations for serving himself were never changed even to clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming restored order but kept an affectation of harsh frugality in his personal habits unchanged.

sentences.zh: 東昏喪道，侈風大扇，哲婦傾城，同符殷、夏，可以垂誡，其在斯乎。

translations.literal: Donghun lost the Way; the wind of extravagance blew greatly; the wise woman overturned the city — the same sign as Yin and Xia; a warning may be hung up — is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun abandoned the Way, luxury ran wild, and a clever woman toppled the state like Jie and Zhou — the lesson hangs here.

sentences.zh: 梁武志在約己，示存宮掖，雖貴嬪之徽華早著，誕育元良，唯見崇重，無聞正位。

translations.literal: Liang Wu's aim was to restrain himself and show regard for the palace women; though the honored consort's splendid beauty was early manifest and she bore and raised the heir apparent, one only sees her honored and heavy — no word of the primary position.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu meant to be sparing; though Ding Guifei bore the heir and was richly honored, he never made her empress.

sentences.zh: 徐妃無行，其殲滅也宜哉。

translations.literal: Consort Xu was without conduct; her destruction was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xu's conduct deserved her ruin.

sentences.zh: 陳武撫茲歸運，奄開帝業。

translations.literal: Chen Wu embraced this returning fortune and suddenly opened imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu seized the turning fortune and founded an empire.

sentences.zh: 若夫儷天作則，燮隆王化，則宣太后其懿焉。

translations.literal: In matching Heaven to make the norm and harmonizing to exalt royal transformation, then Empress Dowager Xuan was the admirable one.
translations.idiomatic: In pairing with Heaven and aiding the throne, Empress Dowager Xuan was the admirable figure.

sentences.zh: 文、宣宮壼，無聞於喪德；

translations.literal: The palaces of Wen and Xuan were without report of conduct that ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The inner courts of Emperors Wen and Xuan heard no scandal of ruinous conduct.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣業，實敗于椒房，既曰牝晨，亦唯家之索也。

translations.literal: The last ruler inherited the enterprise and truly failed in the women's quarters; it is called the hen's morning, and it is also the undoing of the house.
translations.idiomatic: The last ruler inherited the realm and lost it in the women's quarters — the hen crowing at dawn that breaks a house.
